feature: F4 — Wallet & Onboarding, plus the Operator Surface (/ops)

problems.problem: AXIS 1 — Part A is a generic crypto onboarding flow that would be identical for a product with no detection pipeline. A1 (signed-out board), A2 (connect), A3 (funding cliff), A4 (nav chip/account panel), A5 (export) contain exactly one earliness-specific line between them: the intent carry-through preserving {mint, side, amount}. Everything else — two connect paths, a deficit line, three funding tiles, a 3-second export dwell — ships unchanged for a product that starts at the coin. The single place earliness could have lived in Part A is A3, the highest-drop screen, where the user is standing still while the thing they were told they were early to prices in. A3 shows the deficit and never shows the cost of the delay. The dataContract even defines `holding.minutes_early` as 'the number the product is about, and it must be allowed to be negative and shown' — and no screen in this spec shows it.
problems.fix: Put the clock on A3 and A2. A3's deficit line becomes two lines: `You need 1.02 SOL · you have 0.14 SOL` and, from `narratives.promoted_at`, `You're 31m ahead of crypto twitter on $HORN. That was 6m ago.` — a live counter, mono 11px, amber past the 7d p75 (+58m from B2). Order the funding tiles by measured seconds-to-SOL against that counter, not by generic speed. Reuse `.lead-badge` so the number on the funding screen is provably the same number the board showed. And render `minutes_early` on the position row in /you — negative and in `var(--red)` when it was late, per D2.

problems.problem: AXIS 6 — SLI-2 would not have caught the outage it is named for. The spec calls it 'the one that would have caught the two-day outage within minutes' and 'works today with zero schema change'. It does not. `logCycle` is called at the tail of the happy path — `worker/ingest.js:733`, after all lanes, budget adjustment and logging — and is not in a `finally`. B.4 states the 402 threw. A throw skips line 733 entirely, so no row is written to `worker_cycle_log`. SLI-2's `runs` CTE then has zero rows for that worker, and `group by worker` emits no row at all — there is nothing to breach. The query only detects 'ran and produced zero', never 'stopped running', which is the actual failure mode. The replay table (T+4 warn, T+10 page) is false for the incident it replays.
problems.fix: Two changes. (1) Move `logCycle` into a `finally` in every worker so a thrown cycle still writes a row with `ingested: 0` and the error — this is what makes the zero-streak semantics true. (2) Add the absence case to the query, since a worker that dies before it can log anything must still page: left join a fixed `values` list of expected worker names against the CTE and emit `zero_run_streak = 999` when `last_run` is null or older than 3× the stage interval. Absence and zero must both breach; today only zero does, and zero is the case that requires the worker to still be alive.

problems.problem: AXIS 6 — SLI-2's verbatim query pages permanently on two of the four workers that log at all. It reads `coalesce(ingested,0) as out_rows` grouped by worker. `worker/snapshotter.js:376` logs `snapshots_written` and never sets `ingested`; `worker/trends.js:257` logs `refreshed`/`open`/`trend_enriched`, which are not even columns in `worker_cycle_log` (docs/schema.md:159-172 lists only adaptive_floor, budget_note, id, ingested, pruned, ran_at, reads_consumed, skipped_floor, snapshots_written, worker). Both therefore show `zero_run_streak = 999` from the first evaluation onward, forever. Per B.3 that is a DEAD-class page to Slack with @channel, repeating every 15 minutes, ack expiring after 2 hours and re-firing. The alert designed to end alert-blindness manufactures it on day one.
problems.fix: Make `out_rows` per-stage rather than assuming one column means output everywhere: `coalesce(ingested, snapshots_written, refreshed, 0)`, or better, add a single `rows_out int` column to `worker_cycle_log` and have `logCycle` set it from each caller's own output metric. Also fix `worker/trends.js:257` — it is currently inserting keys that do not exist on the table, so that insert is failing and only warning (`cycle-log.js` swallows the error to `console.warn`), meaning `trends` has no cycle history at all right now.

problems.problem: AXIS 2 — the coin-count rule can and will render Buy on an unconfirmed match, and will silently collapse a multi-coin story to one. `narrative_tickers.match_state` is correctly flagged as missing, and A1 defines the primary CTA as `count(narrative_tickers where match_state='CONFIRMED')`. But no build step adds it. Tracing buildOrder: B0, B1, B2, B3, A1, A2, A3, A4, B4, B5, B6, A5 — B5 adds `promoted_at` and `earliness_eligible`, B6 builds the ledger; `match_state` is added by nothing. Meanwhile A1 through A4 ship the board, the trade panel and the real Buy button. The only coin selector that exists is `lib/types.ts:148`: `live.find((c) => c.canonical) ?? live.reduce((a, b) => ((b.mcap ?? 0) > (a.mcap ?? 0) ? b : a))` — canonical if flagged, otherwise whichever mint has the largest market cap. That is precision-by-market-cap, which is the failure mode D1 exists to prevent: on a two-coin story it picks the bigger one and renders `Buy $TICKER` with no ambiguity shown, and on an unverified match it renders Buy because nothing distinguishes unverified from confirmed. ONE RULE is violated for the entire A-track shipping window.
problems.fix: `match_state` moves to B0 as a schema-only change, defaulting every existing row to `'UNSURE'`. Add a pure `primaryAction(narrative)` in `features/coins/model/` that reads only `match_state='CONFIRMED'` counts, returns a discriminated union `{kind:'create'} | {kind:'buy', mint} | {kind:'multi', n}`, and has a mandatory test asserting it never returns `buy` for a zero-CONFIRMED narrative. Every CTA and `.tradebox` mount reads that function and nothing else. Delete or rename `topCoin()` so no surface can reach the mcap fallback — a helper that silently picks a winner must not survive alongside a rule that says the ambiguous state is never rendered.

problems.problem: AXIS 6 — `ops_funnel(ts, stage, platform, arrived, admitted, tracked, triggered, clustered, promoted)` cannot be populated, and the priorArt claim justifying it is false. The spec says 'the six-stage funnel already has the right shape and the right vocabulary; it just needs a table under it.' `worker/lib/funnel-log.js` is a generic `in()/drop(label, remaining)/out()` stepper with arbitrary per-call-site labels, and it has exactly two call sites: `worker/ingest-tiktok.js:265` (`in / stale / views / out`) and `worker/score.js:240` (`in / ranked / pass_meme / out`). Nothing anywhere emits `arrived`, `admitted`, `tracked`, `triggered`, `clustered` or `promoted`. There is no PROMOTE event in the repository at all — grep for `promoted_at|PROMOTE|promote(` across `worker/` and `lib/` returns nothing. So region 2, SLI-6, and `narratives.promoted_at` (called 'the single most important missing column') are all blocked on instrumentation that does not exist, not on a table.
problems.fix: Rewrite B2 from 'persist the funnel' to 'define the funnel'. That means: name the six stage boundaries against real code points (arrived = raw API rows in `ingest.js`, admitted = post-view-floor, tracked = `narrative_posts.tracking_status`, triggered = the tau crossing in `velocity.js`, clustered = `cluster-persist.js` write, promoted = the `display_eligible false→true` transition in `cluster-engine.js`); make PROMOTE an explicit event that stamps `promoted_at` once with a `coalesce(promoted_at, now())` guard so it can never be rewritten on a later cluster cycle; then add the table. Correct the priorArt entry — `FunnelLog` supplies a printing convention, not a taxonomy.

problems.problem: AXIS 5 — the honesty band reads a different clock than the SLI that is supposed to drive it, and the clock it reads has a known corruption that renders a dead pipeline as FRESH. B3 sources every tier from 'SLI-1', which is `max(narrative_posts.first_seen_at)` — our ingest time. But `tier()` in B.5 consumes `PipelineHealth.minutesStale`, and `lib/stories.ts:76-77` computes that from `posted_at`: `Math.round((Date.now() - lastPostAt) / 60_000)` where `lastPostAt` is `narrative_posts.posted_at`, a bigint epoch-ms of when the *author* posted. Two clocks, one band — /ops and the board can disagree about whether the pipeline is alive. Worse, `worker/repair-stale.js` and `worker/schema-repair-stale.sql` exist specifically because `posted_at` has produced 'absurd future dates (double-converted)'. A single future-dated post makes `minutesStale` negative, and `tier()` guards only `minutesStale == null` — so it falls through to `return 'fresh'`, `showLeadClaims` stays true, and every `+31m early` badge renders on a board whose pipeline has been dead for two days. That is exactly the failure B3 was written to prevent, reachable by one bad row.
problems.fix: Change `getTrendingStories` to compute `minutesStale` from `max(first_seen_at)` so the board and SLI-1 are the same query against the same column, and keep `posted_at` for the Age column only (where author time is the correct semantic). Add `if (h.minutesStale < 0) return 'stale'` to `tier()` alongside the null guard — negative freshness is corrupt data, and corrupt data must fail to stale exactly as unknown does. Add both cases to the pure test file the spec already mandates.

problems.problem: AXIS 6 — /ops region 3 lists seven stages, four of which produce no data. The stated rows are `ingest-x, ingest-tt, snapshot, score, cluster, resolve-coins, trends`. The actual `worker` values written to `worker_cycle_log` are `ingest`, `ingest-tiktok`, `snapshotter`, `trends` — none of the spec's names match. `score` and `cluster` never call `logCycle` at all; `resolve-coins` does not exist as a stage anywhere in the repo. On the page whose job is 'name the broken stage without reading a log', four of seven rows are permanently blank, and blank rows on a health table read as healthy.
problems.fix: Take the stage list from the code, not from the mental model: `ingest`, `ingest-tiktok`, `snapshotter`, `score`, `cluster`, `trends`. Add `recordStage()` calls to `score.js` and `cluster.js` in B0 — they are the two stages with no observability at all today, which is worse than the naming mismatch. Drop `resolve-coins` until coin matching exists as a stage. Any stage listed in the UI but never seen in `ops_stage_run` must render `never reported` in `var(--red)`, not empty.

problems.problem: AXIS 5 — the 50 bps Insidor fee is disclosed only on the funding-cliff card tile, i.e. only to users who arrive with no SOL. A3 Tile 2's recap names `−0.5% Insidor` and the mechanism confirms `Insidor referralFee (50 bps; Jupiter keeps 20% of it)`. But the ordinary funded buy never shows it. Per the component inventory §8.8 line 522, the confirm dialog is four rows — Amount / You receive / Price impact / Slippage — with no fee row, and A1's signed-out `.tradebox` spec lists `.recv`, `#recvUsd`, `#minrecv`, `#impact`, `#bal`, `#quoteNote` and again no fee. So the majority path — a user with SOL pressing Buy — never sees what Insidor takes. Fees must be legible on the path most users take, not only on the one screen where the spec happens to be doing arithmetic.
problems.fix: Add a fifth `.r` row to the `.mini` recap in `.tradebox` and a fifth row to the confirm dialog: `Insidor fee` / `0.50% (~0.005 SOL)`, mono, `var(--muted)` label and `var(--ink)` value like every other row — not a footnote, not in `.fine`. Same for the sell side. The `.fine.quote-note` line already has a `live route via Jupiter` state; extend it rather than hiding the fee in it.

problems.problem: AXIS 5 — the create sheet ships a fee split the system does not implement, and the spec knowingly scopes the fix out. The component inventory §9 line 570 has `.split-note` reading 'You earn 3% of every trade as the deployer · Insidor takes 1%', with `.split-bar` hardcoded to `width:60%` / `width:20%`. The dataContract flags this correctly — 'The UI currently asserts a number the system does not implement' against the flow doc's maker 50 / poster 40 / Insidor 10 — then files `poster`/`payout` under 'Not needed for F4'. But A1 explicitly renders `.split` in the signed-out create sheet element list, and A2 ships the create path with `Connect & create $FERRY`. So this feature ships a false financial claim on a screen it is responsible for, having identified the falsehood in its own data contract.
problems.fix: Either implement the split before the create path ships, or replace `.split` with a truthful placeholder for the interim: keep the `.split` skin, drop `.split-bar`, and render one `.split-note` line — `Deployer fee share is not live yet. You will not earn fees on coins created before it ships.` That is an unattractive sentence, which is the point; it is still better than a number that is wrong. Do not ship the 3%/1% markup into the React build.

problems.problem: AXIS 3 — the multi-coin branch of ONE RULE has no screen. A1 specifies the label (`≥2 → See the 3 coins`) and the interaction ('Opens the real sheet (trade or create), fully populated'), but no screen in this spec defines what the N-coins surface is: how the coins are ranked, which columns it carries, whether any of them is buyable from there, how a CONFIRMED and an UNSURE coin sit next to each other in the same list, or what happens when N=2 and one is CONFIRMED and one is UNSURE (which by the rule is a one-CONFIRMED story and should read `Buy $TICKER`, but the count depends entirely on where the abstain band lands). One-third of the product's central rule is a label with nothing behind it.
problems.fix: Specify it as a `.sheet` reusing `.ttable.ntk` (inventory §3.2, grid `28px 2.1fr .62fr .72fr .72fr .82fr`, `min-height:54px`) — rank, ticker, mcap, liquidity, age, and a right-hand action cell. CONFIRMED rows get a `.doit`-scale `Buy` in the action cell; UNSURE rows get the `.nocoin` `unverified` chip and no button, matching A1's abstain treatment. Sort CONFIRMED-first then by `first_deployed` ascending, since temporal ordering is stated as the strongest matching signal — not by mcap, which is the signal that gets front-run.

problems.problem: AXIS 3 — A3's card presets are not deficit-aware and contradict the deficit line directly above them. The worked example is `You need 1.02 SOL · you have 0.14 SOL`, i.e. a 0.88 SOL deficit. Tile 2's presets are `$25 | $50 | $100 | $250` with `$50` default, and the tile's own bottom line reads `$50 in · about $45.90 of $HORN out`. At the spec's own implied SOL price that fills roughly a third of the deficit, so the default path through the highest-drop screen in the product lands the user in the 'partial arrival' state with a $1.95 card fee already paid and a `Buy 0.12 SOL of $HORN instead` downgrade. The screen computes `deficit_sol` and then ignores it when choosing what to offer.
problems.fix: Make the first preset computed: `ceil((deficit_sol * SOL_PRICE) / 5) * 5`, labelled `$195 · covers it` and set as the default `.bchip.on`, with the fixed presets following it. When the computed amount is below the provider minimum, fall back to the minimum and say so. When it exceeds $250, show it anyway rather than silently offering an amount that cannot complete the order the user already expressed.

problems.problem: AXIS 3 — A3's resume contract promises something the mechanism cannot deliver. The `.pendbanner` copy is 'We'll bring you back to $HORN the moment the SOL lands', but the watcher is a client-side `getBalance` poll every 6s in the open tab. If the user closes the tab — which is what people do while waiting on an exchange withdrawal, the tile whose own copy says `arrives in ~30s` but which realistically takes minutes — nothing is watching. The spec's own fallback ('the intent survives a refresh and the toast fires on the next page load') contradicts the promise: it fires when they come back, not when the SOL lands. A broken promise on the screen the spec itself identifies as 'the single highest-drop moment in the product' is the worst place in the design to have one.
problems.fix: Change the copy to what is true: `Leave this tab open and we'll take you straight back to $HORN.` and, when the tab loses visibility, swap the `.lz` line to `Waiting — we'll pick this up when you return.` If the promise is worth keeping, it needs `trade_intent` server-side plus a Helius webhook on the address and a web push — that is a real scope addition and belongs in openQuestions with the localStorage-vs-server question, not assumed by the copy.

problems.problem: AXIS 4 — /ops region 0 is the one place the terminal aesthetic breaks, and it breaks in the direction of a consumer hero. `.ops-verdict` is an 88px strip whose centre is a single word in Clash Display 34px uppercase. Every dense surface in this system runs 12px mono values in `min-height:54px` rows (inventory §3.2 line 142, §4.1 line 158) with 9-11px uppercase micro-labels. A 34px word in an 88px band is roughly six rows of the SLI table spent on one bit of information the operator already has from the dot colour. Compounding it, `animation:pulse 2s` runs 'only when healthy' — motion on the calm state and stillness on the alarm state, which is backwards for a terminal; the eye should be pulled to the thing that needs attention, not away from it.
problems.fix: Collapse region 0 to 54px, matching the table row height so the page is one rhythm. `.ops-state` drops to Clash Display 18px uppercase with the same wide letter-spacing as the micro-labels, keeping the 14px dot as the colour carrier. Reclaim the space for `.ops-why`, which is the sentence that actually names the outage, at mono 12.5px. Move the pulse to DEGRADED and DEAD; healthy is a static lime dot.

problems.problem: AXIS 6 — three tables the spec lists under 'EXISTS AND IS USED AS-IS' do not appear in the live schema probe. `docs/schema.md` is generated from a Supabase service probe on 2026-07-23 and contains no `worker_pipeline_state` and no `worker_crashes`, and its `worker_usage` (lines 174-182) has only `cost_usd, reads_today, source, updated_at, utc_date` — no `cost_breakdown`. All three are defined in SQL (`worker/schema-anthropic.sql`, `worker/schema-cron.sql`, `worker/schema-pipeline-reliability.sql`) but the probe suggests those migrations may not be applied in the environment being probed. SLI-5 reads `worker_pipeline_state.last_run_*`, region 4 reads `worker_usage.cost_breakdown`, and the rail's Errors fallback reads `worker_crashes`.
problems.fix: Verify the applied state before B1 rather than reasoning from the SQL files — the `apply-schema-*.js` scripts exist precisely because application is manual and therefore skippable. Add a `select from information_schema.columns` assertion to the watchdog's own startup so a missing column surfaces as `UNKNOWN` on the verdict strip instead of as an SLI that silently evaluates to null. An SLI querying a nonexistent column is a green board from a dead evaluator, which is the failure mode the spec names as the cause of the original outage.

problems.problem: AXIS 6 — `/api/balance` is an unauthenticated open Helius proxy and this feature multiplies traffic to it. `api/balance.js` accepts any `owner` query param with no auth, no rate limit and no cache (it does not use `api/_lib/cache.js`), and forwards straight to `getBalance` / `getTokenAccountsByOwner` on the project's Helius key. A4 adds a 30s poll per visible tab for every connected user, and A3 adds a 6s poll for up to 15 minutes per funding attempt. Region 4 tracks Helius spend in the ops dashboard but nothing enforces a cap on the route producing it, and the route is callable by anyone with the URL for any address on Solana.
problems.fix: Require a Privy token on `/api/balance` and reject any `owner` that is not a wallet linked to that DID — the balance shown in the nav is by definition the caller's own. Add a 10s server-side cache keyed on owner+mint so the A4 30s poll and A3 6s poll collapse onto it, and stop the 6s poll on `document.visibilitychange`. That also fixes the arithmetic in A3, where '150 credits worst case' assumes a poll that never overlaps with A4's.

problems.problem: AXIS 4/6 — `.dim` still has no CSS rule, and three states in this spec depend on it. The inventory flags it twice (lines 528 and 645): `.dim` is used in `#bal`, the safety-check unknown state and `.inf-soc`, with no rule in `site/index.html`; intended `color:var(--dim)` (#5A5A62). A4 depends on it for `Balance Connect wallet`, for `Balance — SOL` on fetch failure, and for the `no position` and `position unknown` `.pos-badge` variants — the two badges whose entire purpose is to look uncertain. Without the rule they inherit `--ink` #F4F5F7 and render as confident primary text. The dataContract notes the gap; no build step ships the one-line fix.
problems.fix: Add `.dim{color:var(--dim)}` in B0 with the rest of the incident fixes — it is one line and three of this spec's honesty states are wrong without it. While there, note that `.pendbanner` has the same problem (only its `b` is styled); B4 defines the container, which is correct, but B0 is where the `.dim` rule belongs since existing shipped states depend on it today.

problems.problem: AXIS 4 — B2 drops the rail, contradicting B1's own stated rationale. B1 justifies reusing `1fr 460px` because 'the operator is not learning a second layout under stress'. B2 is 'Main only, 1140px, no rail'. The operator moves between these two pages during the same incident — B1's region 0 names a breaching SLI, and SLI-9 (`lead_time_p50`) sends them straight to B2 — and the page reflows under them.
problems.fix: Keep `.rail` on B2 with the same `.railtabs`, defaulting to the `Alerts` tab, so the incident context travels with the operator. If there is genuinely nothing to stream on the earliness page, `.shell.rail-collapsed` already exists (inventory line 360) and collapses without changing the grid definition.

problems.problem: AXIS 3 — A1's localStorage-to-account watchlist merge has no failure or scale states. The element specifies `localStorage['insidor.follow.v1']` merged server-side on connect ('union, never overwrite'), the local key cleared, and a toast `4 saved stories moved to your account`. There is no state for the merge request failing after the local key would be cleared (silent loss of the user's only saved work, on their first authenticated action), no state for a shared or long-lived browser carrying hundreds of stars into a new account, and no state for a user connecting a wallet that already has a server-side follow set from another device.
problems.fix: Clear the local key only on a 2xx from the merge, and on failure keep it and render a `.gate-inline` reading `Your saved stories are still on this device — we couldn't sync them. Retry.` Cap the merge payload at 200 ids, newest first. For the second-device case the union is already correct; just make the toast honest about it — `4 saved stories added · 11 already on your account`.

missing: Story reclassified NEVER-SURFACE under D3 after the user already launched its coin. The spec's own openQuestions #9 admits this state is undecided — 'the coin exists, the wallet holds fees, and the story is gone from every board' — yet A1, A2 and A3 all ship the create path (buildOrder positions 5-7) before it is answered. This is not a rare edge: D3's never-surface tier includes deaths and identifiable private individuals, and a story can cross that line hours after a coin is minted off it. Needs a defined state in /you: does the position row render, does the fee claim still work, what does the user see where the story link was.

Abstain in the trade panel. A1's states list handles abstain at the story level (Buy suppressed, candidate mints shown collapsed with `Possible match: $KANG — we're not confident this is related`), but `.tradebox` has no abstain state anywhere in A1 or A4. If a user reaches the trade panel via a coin route rather than a story route — a `.tk` row, a search result, a shared coin link — nothing in the spec suppresses `.doit`, and the panel has no rendering for 'this mint's link to its story is unverified'.

Negative lead time on any user-facing surface. B2 handles it correctly in the internal ledger (U+2212, `var(--red)`, never absolute-valued, `All` filter default), but no A-screen or B3 tier defines what a negative `.lead-badge` renders on the public board or on a position row. B3 only specifies removing lead badges under stale/fallback — not what a truthful negative badge looks like when the pipeline is fresh and we were simply late. `holding.minutes_early` is defined as 'must be allowed to be negative and shown' and is shown nowhere.

Wrong asset or wrong network arrives during funding. A3 Tile 1 renders a bare address and QR with no network label. States cover partial SOL arrival, no route, and intent expiry, but not: user sent USDC instead of SOL (Tile 3 could catch it but nothing routes them there), user sent from an exchange requiring a memo, or a token arriving that is neither SOL nor swappable. The watcher polls only `getBalance`, so any non-SOL arrival is indistinguishable from nothing arriving.

Card onramp leg 1 succeeds and leg 2 fails. A3's mechanism is explicit that this is two legs, and the states enumerate only the leg-2 failure that happens while waiting ('token became untradeable while waiting'). There is no state for: fiat settled, SOL in the wallet, provider fee already paid, and the Jupiter swap then reverts or the route disappears. The user is left holding SOL they bought at a 3.9% premium specifically to buy a coin they did not get, with no screen acknowledging it.

`.pos-badge` when the story's top coin changes after the comment was posted. The badge is stamped against `story_top_coin_mint` at write time and is explicitly immutable ('It NEVER updates'), which is right. But if the story's top CONFIRMED coin later changes, the badge is a factual claim about a mint the story no longer leads with, rendered next to a coin it does not describe. Needs either the mint symbol inside the badge (`holds 2.1 SOL of $HORN`) or a defined suppression rule.

/ops on a genuinely cold start, before the evaluator has ever run. The 'evaluator stale' state covers `ops_sli_sample` older than 3 minutes, and 'cold start / no baseline' covers funnel `.chgpill`s with under 3 days of history — but not zero rows in `ops_sli_sample` at all, where `latest row per SLI` returns nothing. Region 0's verdict is computed from that query; with no rows it has no worst-breaching SLI and no state, which is the same class of bug as a green board from a dead evaluator.

Interaction between the RECOVERING tier and an in-flight funding intent. B3's recovering state says lead badges 'return only for stories promoted AFTER recovery'. A user who started funding during STALE and completes during FRESH is looking at A3 while the surrounding page changes what it claims. Nothing defines whether their carried intent's story — promoted before recovery, so permanently badge-less — shows a lead claim on the restored `.tradebox`, or what the toast says.

Empty and near-empty list states across /ops. B2 has one ('no CONFIRMED matches at all (fresh install)') and B1 has none: no state for region 3 when no stage has reported, region 4 when `worker_usage` has no rows for today, region 5 when under 24h of gate history exists, or the rail when there are zero alerts, zero errors and zero cycles. On a page whose job is 'tell one person in under three seconds', empty and healthy must not look the same.

First-run signed-out user on the /you tab is specified, but not first-run *connected* user with no holdings, no launches and no follows — the state immediately after A2's Path B mints an embedded wallet. A2 hands to A3 'if an intent was carried', which leaves the no-intent case (user connected from the nav) landing on a /you that A1 only describes in its signed-out form.
